summary: Robert Braden explains that UCLA's computing center did not plan to be a post-office host and only wanted mail for its own staff, which it would print and deliver by courier. He also praises the simple Tenex SNDMSG command, which uses the FTP MAIL command to deliver messages without logging in.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC explains how CCN received mail for its staff and how TENEX's SNDMSG command used FTP MAIL. It also proposes parameters for directing how incoming mail is printed.

subtitle: UCLA-CCN's mail practices and proposed FTP mail extensions.

tldr.problem: UCLA-CCN expected to receive mail for its own staff, not to provide a general post-office service.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes SNDMSG using FTP MAIL and proposes optional parameters for MAIL and MLFL at CCN.
tldr.outcome: The memo says the extended syntax would be implemented by June 1; it does not confirm that implementation occurred.

sections.title: Mail for UCLA-CCN Staff
sections.content: Robert Braden says UCLA-CCN did not plan to provide post-office services and expected to receive mail only for its staff. CCN printed incoming mail and distributed it by courier or secretary to support people who did not regularly use online terminals.
sections.plainLanguage: CCN planned to receive mail for its own staff, print it, and distribute the paper copies. It did not plan to act as a general mail post office.

sections.title: SNDMSG and FTP MAIL
sections.content:
The RFC praises TENEX's SNDMSG command, which uses FTP's MAIL command. To send mail to CCN, a user could address SNDMSG to a name at CCN; the command connects to CCN's FTP and sends a MAIL command followed by the message.

Braden also comments that READMAIL should offer choices such as deleting, keeping, forwarding, or repeating a message.
sections.plainLanguage: SNDMSG could send a message to a CCN address by using the FTP MAIL command. The sender did not need to log in to FTP separately.

sections.title: Proposed Printing Parameters
sections.content:
The RFC proposes extending MAIL and MLFL fields with options for MESSAGE or DOCUMENT, a number of COPIES, and a BIN destination. MESSAGE is the default and prints immediately in uppercase; DOCUMENT queues text for overnight printing in upper and lower case.

Messages would be time- and date-stamped. The RFC says this extended syntax would be implemented by June 1.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposed parameters let a sender choose immediate message printing or overnight document printing, request copies, and select a bin. The RFC states an intended implementation date, not a completed result.
